meta.note: The structure and the words are eidos's sdk/api/v5. kenon's curated text fills what it does not carry.

events.name: game.new
events.when: The player starts a new game, when the first map is set up.

events.name: save.begin
events.when: The game starts writing a save.

events.name: save.done

payload.name: ok
payload.meaning: save.done only: the save was written

events.when: A save has been written (or failed: ok says which).

events.name: save.load

payload.name: play_seconds
payload.meaning: play time of the loaded save

payload.name: state_in_step
payload.meaning: reads 0: whether the mod's own saved data was written with this save is a per-mod answer, and the payload is built once for every handler of the event, so the mod asks the services table's state_in_step (docs/mod-state.md, section 2)

events.when: A save has been read and the game is about to run from it.

events.name: game.cleared
events.where: EVENT_GAMECLEAR_Create 0x0215F8A8, the ending: Hall of Fame (ov180), credits (ov181), save screen (ov205)

payload.name: play_seconds
payload.meaning: play time at the Hall of Fame

events.when: The player beat the Champion; the ending (Hall of Fame, credits, the save screen) starts.

events.name: route.change
events.where: FIELD_MAP_CHANGE_SetupZone 0x021643E8 (ov010, every map change: how warp); the return of FIELDMAP_ChangeZone 0x021893C0 (ov021, a walk over a zone border: how walk)
notes: how is EIDOS_ZONE_WARP (0) for a map change and EIDOS_ZONE_WALK (1) for a walk over a zone border on the same map. A rule that only wants map changes tests event.how == 0.

payload.name: how
payload.meaning: EIDOS_ZONE_WARP (a map change: a door, stairs, a warp tile, Fly, Dig, an Escape Rope, a whiteout, a script) or EIDOS_ZONE_WALK (a walk over a zone border on the same map)

events.when: The player is in a new zone, by any way in: a map change (a door, stairs, a warp tile, Fly, Dig, an Escape Rope, a whiteout, a script) or a walk over a zone border on the same map.

events.name: map.warp
events.when: The player is about to warp to another map (a door, stairs, Fly, a cave exit); the destination can be changed.

events.name: player.step
events.when: The player finished a step on the field.

events.name: trainer.spotted
events.refuse: the trainer does not see the player (the function returns no event)

payload.name: trainer_id
payload.meaning: the trainer who saw the player

payload.name: partner_id
payload.meaning: the second trainer of a double, or 0

events.when: A trainer saw the player and is about to walk up for a battle; refused, the trainer does not see the player.

events.name: npc.talk
events.refuse: no person is found ahead; the A press goes on to the sign and tile checks

payload.name: object_id
payload.meaning: the person or object talked to

events.when: The player pressed A at a person or object; refused, nothing happens.

events.name: menu.open
events.where: EVENT_FIELD_MENU_Create 0x0215FC40 (the X-button menu event) and EVENT_FIELD_MENU_CreateForZone 0x0215FCE0
events.refuse: the menu does not open (no event is returned)
events.when: The player opened the field menu (X); refused, it does not open.

events.name: menu.build
events.modifyText: entries (a cleared entry is hidden; one added is not built)

payload.name: entries
payload.meaning: one bit per menu entry shown

events.when: The field menu lists its entries; the list can be changed.

events.name: field.move
events.refuse: the field action slot answers "not allowed"
events.details: The bag and the Y shortcut menu read these slots: slot 0 is the bicycle; the other slots are zone and tile checks whose items are not mapped yet. Refused, the slot answers "not allowed".  move is the slot number, not a move id.  The party screen's field moves (Cut, Surf, Fly, Dig, Teleport...) do not go through this check and do not fire it yet.

payload.name: move
payload.meaning: the field action slot, 0 to 9 (0 the bicycle); not a move id

events.when: The game checks whether one of its ten field action slots is allowed here (FIELD_SKILL_CHECK_FillUseFlags asks for each, slot 0 to 9).

events.name: pc.open
events.where: SCRCMD_PROC_FLD_CallOv170Event 0x021B4D60, the script command that opens the box screen (the PC, and the battle box with its kind 4)
events.refuse: the PC does not open; the script reads a plain exit
events.details: It is the only way into the box screen.  Refused, it does not open.
events.when: A script opens the Pokemon storage system: a PC (in a Pokemon Centre or anywhere else) or the Battle Box.

events.name: encounter.wild
events.where: the return of FIELD_ENCOUNT_CreateZoneWildMons 0x021A954C; roamers the return of FIELD_ENCOUNT_PickRoamer 0x021A957C
events.refuse: no battle; the player keeps walking; the payload names the area, the method (grass, surf, fishing, shaking grass) and the slot
events.modifyText: species, level, shiny; the second Pokemon of a double; a reroll

payload.name: method
payload.meaning: grass, dark grass, surf, fishing, shaking grass, rippling water, dust

payload.name: reroll
payload.meaning: 1 rolls the encounter again with the game's own roll and fires the event again, at most 16 times; the last answer stands

payload.name: level2
payload.meaning: the second Pokemon of a double (dark grass), 0 when there is none

events.when: A wild Pokemon was rolled on the field, before the battle starts; species, level and shiny can be changed, or the roll done again; refused, there is no encounter.

events.name: encounter.static
events.when: A story or fixed battle with a wild Pokemon is about to start (a legendary, a gift battle); species and level can be changed.

events.name: encounter.trainer
events.when: A trainer battle is about to be set up.

events.name: mon.create

payload.name: nature
payload.meaning: the nature, or 0xFF to leave the roll

payload.name: personality
payload.meaning: the personality value the game rolled

events.when: The game creates a Pokemon (wild, gift, egg, a trainer's); species, level, shiny and nature can be changed.

events.name: mon.receive
events.where: catch EVENT_BATTLE_RETURN_Main 0x021B9614 (ov092, the store step); gifts SCRCMD_PROC_AddMonToParty 0x0215C510, SCRCMD_PROC_AddMonToBox 0x0215C4C8, SCRCMD_PROC_AddEggToParty 0x0215C2D0 (ov010); SCRCMD_POKEMON_FLD_ReceiveGiftMon 0x021B6F18, daycare egg SODATEYA_ReceiveEgg 0x021C32F4 (ov021); in-game trade FLD_TRADE_CreateEvent 0x021CC500 (ov021)

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: catch, gift, static, egg, in-game trade

payload.name: to_box
payload.meaning: it goes to a box because the party is full

events.when: The player gets a Pokemon (a catch, a gift, a static encounter, an egg, a trade), when it is stored.

events.name: mon.nickname
events.modifyText: force the prompt (marked, but the row carries no applier, so a write to it has no effect)

payload.name: mon
payload.meaning: the Pokemon; empty on the prompt's own row, the caught Pokemon on the catch screen's

payload.name: force
payload.meaning: 1 opens the prompt even when the game would skip it (reads 0; the row has no applier)

events.when: The nickname screen opens for a Pokemon (after a catch or from a person).

events.name: mon.evolve
events.refuse: no evolution starts; an evolution stone has no effect
notes: After a battle it fires once for each member that levelled up, before the scene. A refusal skips that member's scene; the others go on.
events.when: The game found that a Pokemon evolves (level, item, trade, friendship), before the evolution scene; refused, it does not evolve.

events.name: mon.exp
events.where: the return of BTL_SERVER_FLOW_CalcPartyExpShares 0x021CB2D4 (ov093); daycare SODATEYA_GrantExp 0x021C3530 (ov021)

payload.name: wild
payload.meaning: for a battle, 1 when the battle is a wild one

events.when: A party Pokemon is about to gain experience (once per member in a battle, or at the day care); the amount can be changed.

events.name: mon.levelup
events.where: the return of BTL_POKEPARAM_AddExp 0x021D69B8, inside BTL_SERVER_FLOW_ApplyPartyExp 0x021C5350 (the level crossing)
notes: For a Rare Candy it fires after the level-up. To stop the candy, refuse item.use.

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: EIDOS_LEVELUP_BATTLE, or EIDOS_LEVELUP_ITEM (a Rare Candy on the party screen)

events.when: A Pokemon reached a new level.

events.name: move.learn
events.where: level-up POKE_TOOL_GetLevelUpMove 0x02018328 (arm9); daycare SODATEYA_LearnMove 0x021C360C (ov021); the party screen's POKELIST_TryLearnMove 0x021BA5B4 and POKELIST_ReplaceMoveSlot 0x021BA5E0 (ov091); the nurse's relearner POKE_SUMMARY_MAIN_ApplyMove 0x021B6B0C (ov173); the script command that writes a move SCRCMD_PROC_SetMonMove 0x0215BD2C (ov010)
events.refuse: the level-up, the day care and the script: the move is not learned. The party screen's rows and the relearner's cannot be refused; the payload names the move and the source

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: level, TM, tutor, relearner; 0 also stands for the rows that name no teacher

payload.name: slot
payload.meaning: the move slot it goes into, or 0xFF when the row names none

events.when: A Pokemon is about to learn a move (level-up, the day care, a tutor); refused, it does not learn it.

events.name: mon.release
events.where: BOX2_MAIN_ClearSlot 0x021DD314, whose only caller is the release step BOX2_SEQ_StateMoveItemF 0x021E81D0, not inside BOX2_MAIN_UpdateBoxSlots
events.refuse: the Pokemon stays; the box redraws it
events.when: The player releases a Pokemon in the storage system; refused, it stays.

events.name: box.deposit
events.where: BOX2_MAIN_UpdateBoxSlots 0x021DD530, a party Pokemon placed in a box
events.refuse: the move is not applied; the box screen's own next step redraws the icons

payload.name: mon
payload.meaning: the Pokemon, where it is now

payload.name: box
payload.meaning: the box it moves into or out of

events.when: The player moves a party Pokemon into a box; refused, it stays in the party.

events.name: box.withdraw
events.where: BOX2_MAIN_UpdateBoxSlots 0x021DD530, a box Pokemon placed in the party
events.refuse: as box.deposit

payload.name: mon
payload.meaning: the Pokemon, where it is now

payload.name: box
payload.meaning: the box it moves into or out of

events.when: The player moves a box Pokemon into the party; refused, it stays in the box.

events.name: party.swap
events.refuse: the order does not change; the party screen redraws from the party
events.when: Two party positions are swapped (the party screen, the storage system); refused, the order stays.

events.name: mon.helditem
events.when: A party Pokemon's held item changes on the party screen.

events.name: egg.hatch
events.when: An egg hatches.

events.name: trade.ingame
events.refuse: the trade does not happen and the script goes on
events.when: A trade with a person in the game is about to happen; refused, there is no trade.

events.name: mon.cure
events.where: PLIST_DEMO_CheckItemUsable 0x021BDD78 (ov091); BTL_SERVER_FLOW_CureSick 0x021C5620 (ov093); after the party heals of heal, for each member they cured
events.refuse: the status stays; an item on the party screen is kept
events.details: status is the game's own number: 1 paralysis, 2 sleep, 3 freeze, 4 burn, 5 poison; in a battle, 6 and up are the battle's own conditions (confusion and the others).  A refusal keeps the status (on the party screen the item is not used; in a battle the game's text may still say it was cured).
notes: A party heal fires it only for members that have a status.

payload.name: status
payload.meaning: 1 paralysis, 2 sleep, 3 freeze, 4 burn, 5 poison; in a battle 6 and up are the battle's own conditions

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: EIDOS_CURE_FIELD_ITEM, _BATTLE (item, move, ability, berry), _PARTY (a party heal)

events.when: A Pokemon's status is about to be cured, by an item, a move, an ability, a berry or a party heal.

events.name: mon.pp
events.refuse: no PP
events.details: amount is the PP it gets, before the cap at its max.  A refusal gives none.
notes: move is 0 when the port cannot read it.

payload.name: move
payload.meaning: the move (0 in a battle for now)

payload.name: amount
payload.meaning: the PP it gets, before the cap at its max

events.when: A move is about to get PP back, from an Ether or an Elixir or in a battle.

events.name: mon.form
events.refuse: the form stays
events.details: A refusal keeps the form it has; to can be changed.

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: EIDOS_FORM_FIELD (an item, the season, a script) or EIDOS_FORM_BATTLE (an ability, a move, a held item)

events.when: A Pokemon is about to change form, outside a battle or in one.

events.name: battle.start
events.where: BTL_SETUP_Create 0x02013090 (arm9); the return of the setups: the wild BTL_SETUP_SetupWild 0x0201347C (arm9), the trainer FIELD_ENCOUNT_SetupTrainerBattle 0x021AA5CC (ov021), the scripted EVENT_BATTLE_CreateScriptedBattle 0x0216E7C8 (ov010)
events.modifyText: format, levels; the payload names the trainer ids and whether the battle is wild

payload.name: wild
payload.meaning: a wild battle; 0 at the row that creates the setup

payload.name: format
payload.meaning: single, double, triple, rotation, multi; 0xFF where the port does not know the format yet (the row that creates the setup)

payload.name: level_adjust
payload.meaning: added to every opposing Pokemon's level

payload.name: opponent_party
payload.meaning: a handle to the opposing party; a handler edits it through the state calls

events.when: A battle is set up and about to start; the format and a level change for the opposing Pokemon can be set.

events.name: battle.action
events.where: fight BTL_CLIENT_IsMoveSelectionBlocked 0x021CF5B0; run BTL_CLIENT_GetEscapeBlockerForSide 0x021CF918 (inside BTL_CLIENT_StepSelectRun); switch the return of BTL_PICK_GetLast 0x0689CB1C (ov095, inside BTL_CLIENT_StepSelectSwitchTarget)
events.refuse: the choice is not accepted and the action menu stays; the payload names the action and, for fight, the move
notes: For a fight it fires several times a turn, once per move checked.

payload.name: side
payload.meaning: 0 the player's, 1 the opponent's (the AI asks the move check too)

events.when: A Pokemon of either side picks its action for the turn (fight, item, switch, run); refused, the choice is not allowed.

events.name: battle.item
events.where: the return of BTLV_CORE_GetSelectedItem 0x021EA01C, inside BTL_CLIENT_StepSelectItem
events.refuse: back to the action menu; the item stays in the bag and the turn is not spent

payload.name: item
payload.meaning: the item chosen from the bag

payload.name: mon
payload.meaning: the Pokemon whose turn it is

payload.name: revive
payload.meaning: the item revives a fainted Pokemon

events.when: The player picked an item from the battle bag; refused, the item is not used.

events.name: battle.switch

payload.name: out
payload.meaning: the Pokemon leaving, or empty after a faint

payload.name: forced
payload.meaning: the switch follows a faint or a move that forces it

events.when: A Pokemon is sent into battle (by choice, after a faint, or forced).

events.name: battle.escape
events.refuse: the escape fails as a failed run: "Can't escape!" and the turn is spent
events.when: A Pokemon tries to run from a wild battle; refused, it cannot escape.

events.name: battle.move
events.when: A Pokemon used a move.

events.name: battle.damage
events.modifyText: the amount; the payload names attacker, target, move and the target's HP before

payload.name: target_hp
payload.meaning: the target's HP before the hit

payload.name: effectiveness
payload.meaning: no effect, not very, neutral, super effective

events.when: A move's damage on one target was worked out, before it is dealt; the damage can be changed.

events.name: battle.faint
notes: mon is a battle reference (place EIDOS_MON_BATTLE); side 0 is the player's. cause, cause_move and cause_damage are empty or 0 when the faint came from weather, a hazard or a status.
A whiteout has its own event, whiteout. It is not the same moment as a single faint.
Poison on the field never faints a Pokemon in this game (it stops at 1 HP).

payload.name: cause_damage
payload.meaning: the last damage, or 0 for weather, a hazard or a status

events.when: A Pokemon fainted in a battle.

events.name: catch.attempt
events.refuse: the ball is blocked as in a trainer battle: the block message shows, the ball stays in the bag, the turn is spent; the payload names the ball and the target's species and level

payload.name: rate
payload.meaning: the catch rate the roll uses, as a percentage of the game's own factor

payload.name: static
payload.meaning: 1 when encounter.static started the battle (a story or fixed Pokemon), 0 for a wild roll

events.when: The player throws a ball; the catch rate can be changed; refused, the throw does nothing.

events.name: catch.result
events.when: A thrown ball shook and the catch succeeded or failed.

events.name: battle.end
events.when: A battle ended (won, lost, ran, caught).

events.name: whiteout

payload.name: in_battle
payload.meaning: 1 the battle half, 0 the field half

events.when: The player lost a battle with no Pokemon left (the battle half) and is taken back to heal (the field half).

events.name: battle.trainer_mon
events.where: the rows that build a trainer battle's setup (battle.start), once per opposing member
events.refuse: the member leaves the party (the last stays)
events.modifyText: species, level, item, moves, ability, form
events.details: It fires once per member, in party order.  A refusal takes the member out of the party (the last one always stays).  A changed field is written to the Pokemon with the game's own setters: a new species or level works out the stats again, a new move gets its full PP.  0 in a *mod field leaves the game's value.

payload.name: index
payload.meaning: the position in the party, 0 first

events.when: A trainer battle is about to start: once for each Pokemon of the opposing trainer's party.

events.name: battle.exp
events.where: the return of BTL_SERVER_FLOW_CalcPartyExpShares 0x021CB2D4 (ov093), before mon.exp
events.refuse: nobody gains
events.details: It fires before mon.exp fires for each member that gains.  A refusal gives nobody any experience (and mon.exp does not fire); scale changes every member's share.
notes: members has bit i set for each party position i that gains. scale is a percentage of every share: 100 leaves them. To change one member only, use mon.exp.

payload.name: members
payload.meaning: bit i: party position i gains

payload.name: scale
payload.meaning: a percentage of every share; 100 leaves them

events.when: The battle is about to hand out experience to the party after an opposing Pokemon fainted.

events.name: item.add
notes: It cannot be refused. Set count to 0 to keep the item out of the bag; the game's text still says it was received.

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: EIDOS_ITEM_FROM_SCRIPT (an item on the ground, a gift from a person), _GIFT, _PURCHASE, _BATTLE, _RETURN (a held item or mail back to the bag), _REWARD, _OTHER

events.when: An item is about to go into the bag; the count can be changed.

events.name: item.use
events.refuse: the game's "it won't have any effect"; the item stays
events.details: Items used straight from the bag on the field (Escape Rope, Repel, the bicycle, the Dowsing Machine) do not go through the party screen and do not fire this event yet.

payload.name: target
payload.meaning: the Pokemon it is used on, or empty

events.when: The party screen checks whether an item works on a Pokemon, before it is used; refused, the item has no effect and stays in the bag.

events.name: shop.buy
events.refuse: back to the item list; no money changes hands

payload.name: price
payload.meaning: the price of one; the shop shows and charges it

events.when: The player picked an item in a shop, before choosing how many; the price of one can be changed; refused, the shop goes back to its list.

events.name: money.change
notes: source says why: a script, a purchase, a sale or a battle. A handler may change the amount only in the direction of the call.

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: EIDOS_MONEY_SCRIPT, _PURCHASE, _SALE, _BATTLE (a prize when the delta is positive, a loss when it is negative), _OTHER

events.when: The player's money is about to go up or down; the change can be changed.

events.name: heal
events.where: SCRCMD_PROC_HealParty 0x0215B5A8 (ov010, a centre or a script); GPOWER_UseHpRestore 0x0201104C (arm9, the HP-restore power)
events.refuse: the heal does not happen; the script's own text still plays
notes: Refused, the whole heal does not happen: no member event fires. To spare one member, see mon.revive and heal.hp.
script_id is the id of the script that runs the heal. The Pokemon Centre nurse runs one script of her own, so a mod tells her heal from the others by that id. The nurse's id is not named yet.

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: Pokemon Centre or script, the HP-restore power

payload.name: mask
payload.meaning: one bit per party position to heal

payload.name: script_id
payload.meaning: for a script heal, the id of the script that heals (the Centre's nurse runs one script of her own); 0 for the power

events.when: The whole party is about to be healed (a Pokemon Centre or another script, the HP-restore power); refused, nobody is healed.

events.name: heal.hp
events.where: PLIST_DEMO_RestoreHp 0x021BE914 (ov091, an item on the field); BTL_SERVER_FLOW_ApplyHpRecover 0x021C33E8 (ov093, every restore in a battle); after the party heals of heal, for each member they gave HP to
events.refuse: no HP is added
events.details: The amount is the HP the game is about to add, before the cap at max_hp; a handler changes it, or refuses the event and the Pokemon gets nothing.  A fainted Pokemon coming back is mon.revive, not this event.  On the field the item is still used up: a mod that wants the item kept refuses item.use instead.
notes: source is 0 (EIDOS_HEAL_HP_FIELD) on the field and 1 (EIDOS_HEAL_HP_BATTLE) in a battle. A party heal fires it once for each member that has lost HP, with source EIDOS_HEAL_HP_PARTY.

payload.name: mon
payload.meaning: the Pokemon that gets HP back

payload.name: amount
payload.meaning: the HP to add, before the cap at max HP

payload.name: source
payload.meaning: field (an item from the bag or the party screen) or battle (any restore: bag item, held item, move, ability)

events.when: A Pokemon that has HP is about to get more, from an item, a move, an ability, a held item or a party heal.

events.name: mon.revive
events.where: PLIST_DEMO_CheckItemUsable 0x021BDD78 and PLIST_DEMO_RestoreHp 0x021BE914 (ov091); BTL_SERVER_FLOW_ItemEffectRevive 0x021CC008 (ov093); after the party heals of heal, for each member they revived
events.refuse: the Pokemon stays fainted; an item is kept where the game allows (docs/mod-payloads.md)
events.details: A refusal keeps it fainted; for an item, the item is not used up.  The hp is what it comes back with, at least 1, at most max_hp.
notes: source says what brought it back: EIDOS_REVIVE_FIELD_ITEM, _BATTLE_ITEM, _MOVE, _CENTRE, _POWER or _SCRIPT. The port reports every script heal as _SCRIPT, the Centre's too, because the nurse runs the same script command.

payload.name: hp
payload.meaning: the HP it comes back with; at least 1, at most max_hp

events.when: A fainted Pokemon is about to come back, from a revive item, Sacred Ash or a party heal.

events.name: badge.get
events.when: The player gets a gym badge.

events.name: flag.set
events.when: A story flag is set or cleared.

events.name: dex.register
events.when: A species is registered in the Pokedex as seen or caught.

blocks.text: A raw hook replaces or wraps one game function from the list below. It is for code mods only, with the game's own arguments. Prefer events and rules; use a hook when no event covers what you need.
In kenon, one hook is one line in the Hooks view: `region:address mode symbol`. The symbol is a function exported by your mod's code.
ov093:0x021CBD48 wrap my_catch_rate sig="int (void)" switch=my_catch

items: `wrap` runs your function in place of the game's and lets you call the original through the chain. Several wraps nest, the last loaded runs first.
`replace` takes the function for itself. When two mods replace one function, the later mod wins and the other is reported as shadowed.
`sig` states the prototype you expect, as `"<return> (<parameters>)"`. The port refuses the hook when it differs from the function's own.
A hook is keyed by region and address, never by name, because names change when the decompilation is cleaned up.
The game's arguments can change when the code is restructured. A mod with raw hooks states the port version it was built for.

blocks.text: Rows with events are already bound to a stable event: that event fires from the same function.

A code mod is C built to WebAssembly. It exports eidos_mod_start and eidos_mod_stop, binds handlers to events with `eidos_on`, and reaches the game only through the calls of eidos_wasm.h. It cannot call game functions directly; raw hooks replace or wrap them.

A handler gets a copy of the event payload and returns EIDOS_EVENT_CONTINUE or EIDOS_EVENT_REFUSE. It may write the payload fields marked writable; the port reads them back before the game goes on. A write to any other field has no effect. A refusal at an event that cannot be refused is ignored and logged once.

items: The snippets in these docs build as they are with the Code view's template: `#include "eidos_wasm.h"`, the constants are spelled EIDOS_, and the payload structs are Eidos<Name>.
A handler is registered by its function table index. In C that is its address: `eidos_on(EIDOS_EVENT_MON_EXP, (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)on_exp)`.
A Pokemon reference (EidosMonRef) goes to a state call as its five fields: handle, place, side, box and slot.
No libc and no WASI: a mod reaches nothing outside the game except through the port's imports. The template brings a small allocator and the memory functions.

blocks.text: Several handlers on one event all run, in load order. Writes chain and any refusal refuses. The battle works on a copy of each Pokemon: during a battle read and write the battle record (battle_get, battle_set), not the party record.
The core imports come from the module `eidos`.

head: Call
What it does
rows: `void eidos_log(const char *text, uint32_t len)`
Writes a line to the port's mod log. Pass the text and its length.
`int32_t eidos_on(uint32_t kind, uint32_t handler_index)`
Binds a handler to an event by the event's id. The handler is a function table index: in C, the handler's address cast to uint32_t. Call it from eidos_mod_start.
`int32_t eidos_script(uint32_t vm, uint32_t opcode, uint32_t handler_index)`

Binds a handler to a script command of one of the two script machines. vm is an EIDOS_SCRIPT_VM_* constant, opcode the command, and the handler a function table index. The handler returns an EIDOS_SCRIPT_* answer.
`int32_t eidos_override(uint32_t region, uint32_t addr, uint32_t handler_index)`
Binds a handler to a game function from the raw hook list, by region and address. The handler is a function table index.
`int64_t eidos_original(const uint32_t *args, uint32_t nargs)`
Inside a hook handler, calls the next link of the chain (the game's own function, or the next wrap) with the arguments in args, and returns its result. Pass the argument count in nargs.
`uint32_t eidos_rd8(uint32_t ds_addr)`
Reads a byte of game memory at a DS address. The access is bounds-checked.
`uint32_t eidos_rd16(uint32_t ds_addr)`
Reads 16 bits of game memory at a DS address.
`uint32_t eidos_rd32(uint32_t ds_addr)`
Reads 32 bits of game memory at a DS address.
`void eidos_wr8(uint32_t ds_addr, uint32_t value)`
Writes a byte of game memory at a DS address. The access is bounds-checked.
`void eidos_wr16(uint32_t ds_addr, uint32_t value)`
Writes 16 bits of game memory at a DS address.
`void eidos_wr32(uint32_t ds_addr, uint32_t value)`
Writes 32 bits of game memory at a DS address.
`int32_t eidos_read(uint32_t ds_addr, void *dst, uint32_t len)`
Copies len bytes of game memory from a DS address into the mod's memory.
`int32_t eidos_write(uint32_t ds_addr, const void *src, uint32_t len)`
Copies len bytes of the mod's memory into game memory at a DS address.

blocks.text: The module exports:

items: `eidos_mod_start`: 0 when the mod started.
`eidos_mod_stop`
`memory`: The linear memory.
`__indirect_function_table`: The function table the handler indices point into.

blocks.text: Players join one session through the game's Session page. The host's game decides what is shared. Each player's own events stay on that player's game.
A mod that takes part in multiplayer states a compatibility number in the manifest. Mod settings writes it as Multiplayer version.
multiplayer = 3

items: The number is a whole number from 1. A value that is not one is ignored.

The lobby lets the players start only when everyone's multiplayer mods have the same numbers. Only the number has to match, so a mod can update freely while its messages stay the same. Raise the number when they change.
A mod with no `multiplayer` line is not checked by the lobby.
A code mod reaches a session with `session_host`, `session_join`, `session_leave` and `session_send`, and receives joins, leaves and messages in the handler it sets with `on_session`.
Rules cannot use multiplayer yet. Use a code mod.

blocks.text: Other players' events. The host's mod gets every event that another player's game fires, in the usual handler for that event. `event_player` says whose event it is: 0 for this game's own, else the player's number in the session.

items: A remote event cannot be refused or changed, because the other game has already acted on it. A refusal or a write is ignored.
A Pokemon reference in another player's payload names a Pokemon of that game, not of this one.
Each game sends its events and its position in batches, at most 10 times a second.

blocks.text: The shared table. It holds numbers that every player's mods see, such as a count or a pair of Pokemon. `shared_set(key, value)` writes one, `shared_get(key, &value)` reads one, `shared_add(key, delta)` adds to one and `shared_cas(key, expected, value)` sets one only if it still holds the expected number. The keys belong to the mod, so two mods can use the same key.

items: The host's copy is the real one and is kept with its game. A joiner's change goes to the host, which applies the changes in the order they come and sends each one to every player. A joiner reads its own change once the host has sent it back.
`shared_get` returns 0 when the key is set, 1 when it is not, and -1 outside a multiplayer game.
`shared_set` replaces the value, so when two players set the same key at the same moment the later one wins. Use `shared_add` for counters: every change counts.
Use `shared_cas` to set a value only if nobody changed it. It is not answered: read the key afterwards to see whether it took.
The writers return 0 when the change was made (host) or sent (joiner), and -1 outside a multiplayer game or for a key that cannot be sent (empty, over the limit, or with a space).

blocks.text: Recipes: Count faints of all players, Log another player's catch.
A rule acts on one event without any code. It has an event, zero or more guards (`when`) and one or more actions (`do`). It has no loops, functions, local variables or branches.
A rule file holds one rule. The manifest binds the file to its event with a `rule = <event> <path>` line; the event in the file must match.

language 1
rule faint_penalty on battle.faint
    when event.side == 0
    do sub money 1000

items: Several `when` lines must all hold.
A rule that reaches 256 steps stops for that firing without refusing.
Division or modulo by zero gives 0. An unset cell reads 0.
Several mods on one event all run, in load order. Writes chain and any refusal refuses.

blocks.text: Need a loop, a search of the party, a fallback or anything beyond this? Write a code mod; the two mix in one mod.

Read a payload field as `event.<field>`. Read the game through state fields such as `money` or `level[event.mon]`. Keep your own data in `state.<cell>`; with a subscript it is a keyed table, up to 1024 keys, saved with the game.

head: Type
Values
rows: int
A 32-bit signed number. Every numeric payload and state field.
bool
true or false. Comparisons and flag fields.
text
A string literal.
mon
A Pokemon reference. Use it as a subscript: hp[event.mon].

blocks.text: Operators, loosest to tightest: `||`, `&&`, `!`, comparisons (`== != < <= > >=`), `+ -`, `* / %`, unary `-`. Both sides of a comparison must have the same type; arithmetic needs int. There are no names for enum values: use the numbers listed on the event page.
Read the mod's own options as `setting.<key>` (see Options) and its data tables as `table.<name>[key]`.
Operators are read as two characters at most. A pair that is not an operator reads as two, so `x*-1` and `a<-1` mean what they look like.

head: Target
Writable when
rows: event.<field>
The payload page marks the field writable. Any other field is a load error.
money, hp[m], battle_style
The state field page says the port can write it.
state.<cell>, state.<cell>[key]
Always. The cell belongs to your mod.

blocks.text: The game's later write wins. To make a change stick, write the payload field of the event the game derives the value from, not the state field after it.
A table is a file of numbers the mod reads by key: a level cap for each badge count, a list of banned species, a zone-to-area map. Rules and code read it. What the table means is up to the mod.
Declare each table with one line in the manifest. The Tables view writes it for you.
table = caps tables/caps.txt

items: The name is letters, digits and `_`, does not start with a digit, and has at most 31 characters.
The path is inside the mod folder.
A mod can hold up to 128 tables in all, counting every loaded mod.
A table belongs to the mod that declares it. Two mods can each have a table called `caps`; neither reads the other's.

blocks.text: The file has one entry per line. A key and a value are signed 32-bit numbers, written in decimal or with `0x` for hex. `#` starts a comment. `default = N` is the value of every key the table does not list, and 0 when there is no such line.

# level cap per badge count
0 = 12
1 = 20     # after the first gym
0x2 = 25
default = 100

items: When a key is listed twice, the later line wins. The checker warns about it.
A table holds up to 65536 entries, and the file is at most 16 MiB.
A table that fails to load is reported when the game starts. The mod's other tables and rules still load.

blocks.text: A rule reads a table with `table.<name>[key]`. The key is any number expression, such as `badges`. A key the table lacks reads the default.

language 1
rule level_cap on mon.exp
    when level[event.mon] >= table.caps[badges]
    do set event.amount 0
A rule that names a table the mod does not declare is refused when the game loads it. The checker reports the same error. Code reads a table with `table_get(name, key, &out)`.

A mod can show options on the game's settings screen, under its own name. The player picks a value, the game keeps it beside the mod's saved data, and the mod reads it. Declare the options in a file and name it in the manifest. The Options tab of Mod settings writes both.
settings = options.txt
The file has one option per line: `option <key> <kind> "<label>" <value>`. `#` starts a comment, except inside the quoted label. A line that does not start with `option` is skipped.

option dupes   bool    "Dupes clause"    on
option cap     choice  "Level caps"      off|gym|ace
option lives   int     "Lives"           0 10 3

head: Kind
Value
Reads as
rows: bool
`on`, `off`, `true`, `false`, `1` or `0`. Any other text is reported and the option is ignored.
1 or 0
choice
Names split by `|`, 31 characters each, as many as you want. The first is the default.
The index of the chosen name
int
`<min> <max> <default>`, whole numbers within a billion of zero, with min <= default <= max. The screen steps by one.
The number

items: The key is one word. It cannot hold a space, `=`, `#` or a quote, and it has at most 63 characters. Dots are allowed.
The label is quoted, has no quote, and has at most 63 characters.
A mod can declare any number of options.
A line the game cannot read is reported and ignored. The checker reports it too.
When a key is declared twice, the game reports it and ignores the second.

blocks.text: A rule reads an option with `setting.<key>`. A rule reads a dotted key as written: `setting.nuzlocke.dupes`. Each word of a key is letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit. A key the mod does not declare reads -1, and the checker warns about it. A mod with no namespace has no settings, and the game refuses a rule that reads one. Code reads an option with `setting_get(key)`.

language 1
rule lives on catch.attempt
    when setting.lives == 0
    do refuse
What a mod cannot do yet with API ${apiVersion}.

items: Tell how the player entered a zone (door, Fly, Dig, Escape Rope, whiteout...). `route.change` only says walk or map change.
Tell which box screen opened (organise, deposit, withdraw, Battle Box).
Block or see items used straight from the bag: Escape Rope, Repel, bicycle, Dowsing Machine.
Block or see Cut, Surf, Fly, Dig, Teleport and other moves used from the party screen.
Refuse an item the player receives. Setting the count to 0 keeps it out of the bag, but the message still shows.
Tell a Pokemon Centre heal by name. Compare `heal.script_id` with the nurse's script id instead.
See how many of an item the player buys at the moment they pick it.
Make a Pokemon disobey, for example above a level cap.
Change type effectiveness in battle.
Read or set a nickname, or force the nickname screen after a catch.
Read a trainer's class, party size or highest level, or whether a trainer was beaten.
Tell which party Pokemon took part in a battle.
Block the Day Care, trades, the Entralink or Dream World sync.
Block a Pokemon joining the party.
Give the player a new Pokemon or egg made by the mod.
Export a Pokemon to a file and import it again, for example to carry a team to the next game.
Receive messages from another game in a rule.
Read a zone's wild encounter slots.
Hook the link and minigame screens. Items from them report source `OTHER`.
Add moves past 560 with their own battle animations.
Add new overworld characters.
Add species past the original ones, up to 2047.
Replace a game function from a code mod. `eidos_override` and `eidos_original` answer -1 for now; native mods can.
Receive a save sent by a peer in a code mod. `on_save_received` does nothing yet.
Cap a code mod's memory or running time. A runaway mod can slow the game.
A `player.step` mod does not fire in a build made from the decompiled source.

recipes.title: Lose money when a Pokemon faints
recipes.goal: Take 1000 money each time one of your Pokemon faints.
steps: `battle.faint` fires when a Pokemon faints. `event.side` is 0 for the player's side.
The rule guards on the side and subtracts from `money`.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule faint_penalty on battle.faint
    when event.side == 0
    do sub money 1000

recipes.title: Cap the level
recipes.goal: Stop a Pokemon from gaining experience once it reaches level 30.
steps: `mon.exp` fires before experience is added. `event.level` is the level before; `event.amount` is writable.
Setting the amount to 0 in the rule keeps the battle, the display and the saved Pokemon in agreement.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule level_cap on mon.exp
    when event.level >= 30
    do set event.amount 0
notes: Refusing `mon.levelup` instead would leave the screen showing a level the Pokemon does not have; lower the experience.

recipes.title: Block grass encounters before the first badge
recipes.goal: No wild battle in grass while the player has no badge.
steps: `encounter.wild` can be refused. `event.method` is 0 for grass.
`badges` is a state field with the number of badges.
A refused encounter is no battle; the player keeps walking.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_early_grass on encounter.wild
    when badges == 0 && event.method == 0
    do refuse

recipes.title: Make low-level Pokemon easier to catch
recipes.goal: Double the catch rate for wild Pokemon below level 20.
steps: `catch.attempt` fires when a ball is thrown. `event.level` is the target's level.
`event.rate` is the catch rate as a percentage of the game's own: 100 leaves it alone, 200 doubles it. It is a byte, so 255 is the most.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule easy_catch on catch.attempt
    when event.level < 20
    do set event.rate 200

recipes.title: Show a message on a level-up
recipes.goal: Tell the player when a Pokemon reaches a level that is a multiple of 10.
steps: `mon.levelup` fires once for the level crossing. `event.to` is the level reached.
`message` shows text in the game's window. The text is a fixed string.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule round_level on mon.levelup
    when event.to % 10 == 0
    do message "A round number!"

recipes.title: Pay a bonus for beating a trainer
recipes.goal: Add 500 money when the player wins a trainer battle.
steps: `battle.end` carries `outcome` (0 is a win) and `wild` (0 for a trainer battle).
The rule adds to `money`.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule trainer_bonus on battle.end
    when event.outcome == 0 && event.wild == 0
    do add money 500
notes: `money.change` does not say where money came from, so a rule that doubles prize money there would also double other income. Test before relying on it.

recipes.title: Every fished Pokemon is shiny
recipes.goal: Make fishing encounters shiny.
steps: `encounter.wild` lets a rule write `event.shiny`: 1 forces shiny, 0 leaves the roll.
`event.method` is 3 for fishing.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule shiny_fishing on encounter.wild
    when event.method == 3
    do set event.shiny 1

recipes.title: Forbid releasing Pokemon from the PC
recipes.goal: The release step does nothing and tells the player why.
steps: `mon.release` fires on the release step of the box screen and can be refused. The Pokemon stays; the box redraws it.
A refusal shows nothing by itself: add a `message`.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule keep_everyone on mon.release
    do refuse
    do message "These Pokemon stay."

recipes.title: One catch per route
recipes.goal: Allow one catch on each zone, then refuse more balls there.
steps: Two rules share a keyed cell: `state.route_used[zone]`. Cells are saved with the game.
`catch.result` sets the cell when `event.caught` is 1.
`catch.attempt` can be refused: the ball stays in the bag and the turn is spent.
A rule file holds one rule, so these are two files.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule mark_route_used on catch.result
    when event.caught == 1
    do set state.route_used[zone] 1
recipes.rule2:
language 1
rule one_catch_per_route on catch.attempt
    when state.route_used[zone] == 1
    do refuse
    do message "You already caught a Pokemon on this route."
notes: The first block is the rule for `catch.result`; the second is the rule for `catch.attempt`.

recipes.title: A setting that switches a feature
recipes.goal: Halve all experience when the player turns on an option in the port's settings screen.
steps: Declare the option in an options file and name it in the manifest with `settings = options.txt`. The Options tab of Mod settings writes both.
A rule reads the option as `setting.<key>`. It is 0 or 1 for a bool, the index for a choice.
In C, the handler for `mon.exp` reads the option with `setting_get`.
`amount` is writable, so both halve it before the game uses it.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule slow_exp on mon.exp
    when setting.slow_exp == 1
    do set event.amount event.amount / 2

recipes.title: Release a Pokemon when it faints
recipes.goal: A fainted Pokemon of the player is released for good (a Nuzlocke rule).
steps: `battle.faint` fires when a Pokemon faints. `event.side` is 0 for the player's side and `event.mon` is the fainted Pokemon.
`release` (in C, `mon_release`) queues the release. It is applied at the first player step on the field after the battle, so the battle is not disturbed.
It does nothing if the Pokemon is the last one that is not an egg.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule nuzlocke on battle.faint
    when event.side == 0
    do release event.mon
notes: Whiteout is a separate event, `whiteout`. Poison on the field does not faint a Pokemon in this game.

recipes.title: Give an item on entering a map
recipes.goal: Give 5 Potions the first time the player enters a zone.
steps: `route.change` fires whenever the player enters a new zone, by a map change or by walking over a zone border; `event.zone` is the zone entered. Replace 115 with the zone you want.
`give <item> <count>` puts the items in the bag at once. If the bag cannot take them, the rule stops for that firing and tries again on the next entry.
The cell `state.gift_given` is saved with the game and reads 0 until it is set, so the gift is given once. The `give` line comes first, so the cell is set only after a successful gift.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule potion_gift on route.change
    when event.zone == 115 && state.gift_given == 0
    do give 17 5
    do set state.gift_given 1
notes: The C version keeps its flag in memory only. Save it with `state_store` to keep it across runs. `item_count[17]` reads the Potions the bag holds, for a rule that gives only when the bag has none.

recipes.title: Halve all healing
recipes.goal: Every HP restore gives half the HP, on the field and in battle.
steps: `heal.hp` fires before HP is added. `event.amount` is the HP to add and is writable.
The amount is capped at max HP after the rule runs.
`event.source` is 0 on the field and 1 in battle, so a `when` line can limit the rule to one of them.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule half_healing on heal.hp
    do set event.amount event.amount / 2

recipes.title: No HP restores in battle
recipes.goal: No Pokemon gets HP back during a battle, from any source.
steps: `heal.hp` can be refused; a refusal adds no HP. In battle it fires for every restore: bag items, berries, Leftovers, moves and abilities.
`event.source` is 1 for a battle.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_battle_healing on heal.hp
    when event.source == 1
    do refuse
notes: A bag item is still used up when its restore is refused. To stop the item from being used, refuse `battle.item`: the player returns to the action menu.

recipes.title: Count faints in the status panel
recipes.goal: Show how many of your Pokemon fainted this session beside the screens.
steps: `battle.faint` fires for both sides; `side` 0 is the player's.
`panel_set` writes one of the 16 panel lines.

recipes.title: Level cap by badge
recipes.goal: A Pokemon gains no experience once it reaches the level cap for the badges the player holds.
steps: Make a table called `caps` in the Tables view. Each key is a badge count and each value the highest level allowed. `default` covers every count the table does not list.
`mon.exp` fires once for each party member that gains experience. Setting `event.amount` to 0 gives that member none.
`table.caps[badges]` reads the cap for the badges the player holds now.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule level_cap on mon.exp
    when level[event.mon] >= table.caps[badges]
    do set event.amount 0
notes: The cap compares the level before the gain, as `event.level` and `level[event.mon]` both read it.

recipes.title: Rare Candy stops at the cap
recipes.goal: A Rare Candy cannot be used on a Pokemon that has reached the level cap.
steps: `item.use` fires when the party screen checks an item on a Pokemon, and can be refused. A refusal keeps the Rare Candy in the bag and the level as it was.
`event.item` is the item and `event.target` the Pokemon it is used on. Item 50 is the Rare Candy in the game's item list.
The cap comes from the `caps` table of the level cap recipe.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule candy_cap on item.use
    when event.item == 50 && level[event.target] >= table.caps[badges]
    do refuse
    do message "It cannot grow past the cap yet."

recipes.title: Roll again for a species the player owns
recipes.goal: A wild encounter of a species the player already owns is rolled again.
steps: `owned[s]` is 1 when the party or a box holds a Pokemon of species `s` that is not an egg.
`event.reroll` is writable. Setting it to 1 rolls the encounter again with the game's own roll and fires the event again, at most 16 times. The last roll stands.
A rule that refuses the event on a reroll leaves no encounter.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule dupes on encounter.wild
    when owned[event.species] == 1
    do set event.reroll 1
notes: To skip only the first stage of an evolution line, add `species_stage[event.species] == 0` to the guard. To count a whole evolution line as one species, see the recipe on evolution lines.

recipes.title: Dupes clause by evolution line
recipes.goal: A wild encounter is rolled again when the player already has a Pokemon of the same evolution line in the party, or any stage of it in a box.
steps: `species_base[s]` is the first stage of the evolution line of species `s`. Two species are in one line when their bases are equal, so Charmander, Charmeleon and Charizard share a base.

A rule compares the base of the rolled species with the base of each party member. A rule has no loops, so the guard lists the six party positions. `species[k]` with a number `k` reads the Pokemon in party position `k`, and `party_count` keeps the empty positions out.
A rule cannot read the boxes one by one. The code version below checks the party and every box.
`event.reroll` rolls the encounter again; the last roll stands.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule dupes_by_line on encounter.wild
    when party_count > 0 && species_base[species[0]] == species_base[event.species] || party_count > 1 && species_base[species[1]] == species_base[event.species] || party_count > 2 && species_base[species[2]] == species_base[event.species] || party_count > 3 && species_base[species[3]] == species_base[event.species] || party_count > 4 && species_base[species[4]] == species_base[event.species] || party_count > 5 && species_base[species[5]] == species_base[event.species]
    do set event.reroll 1
notes: An empty box slot makes box_ref fail, so the loop skips it. A box holds 30 slots.

recipes.title: Block revive items in battle only
recipes.goal: Revive items work on the party screen but not from the bag in battle.
steps: `mon.revive` fires when a fainted Pokemon is about to come back. `event.source` tells what brought it: 0 is an item on the party screen, 1 is a revive item in battle, 2 a move or ability, 3 a Centre, 4 the HP-restore power, 5 any other script heal.
The rule guards on source 1 and refuses. In battle a refused revive item has no effect and the bag keeps the item.
Every other source goes on as usual.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_battle_revives on mon.revive
    when event.source == 1
    do refuse
notes: What a refusal does depends on the source: an item on the party screen says it has no effect and stays in the bag, Sacred Ash is used up and that member stays fainted, and a party heal leaves that member fainted and heals the others.

recipes.title: No party heals
recipes.goal: Pokemon Centres, scripts and the HP-restore power heal nobody.
steps: `heal` is the whole party heal. A rule that refuses it stops the heal: no member event fires and nobody is healed.
A script's own text still plays.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_party_heals on heal
    do refuse
notes: To spare one member and heal the rest, refuse `mon.revive` (a fainted member) or `heal.hp` (a hurt one) for that member.

recipes.title: Block status cures in battle only
recipes.goal: Status cures work on the party screen but not from the bag in battle.
steps: `mon.cure` fires when a status is about to be cured. `event.source` is 0 for an item on the party screen, 1 in a battle and 2 for a party heal.
The rule guards on source 1 and refuses. The status stays, and every other source goes on as usual.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_battle_cures on mon.cure
    when event.source == 1
    do refuse
notes: A refused cure in a battle can still show the game's text that the status was cured. To stop the item from being used, refuse `battle.item`.

recipes.title: Halve PP restores
recipes.goal: Every PP restore gives half the PP, on the field and in battle.
steps: `mon.pp` fires before PP is added. `event.amount` is the PP the move gets, and is writable.
The amount is capped at the move's maximum after the rule runs. A refusal gives no PP.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule half_pp on mon.pp
    do set event.amount event.amount / 2

recipes.title: One Pokemon is not healed by a party heal
recipes.goal: A party heal heals everyone except Pokemon of species 25.
steps: A party heal fires `heal.hp` once for each member that has lost HP, with source 2, and `mon.revive` once for each fainted member. A refusal affects that member only.
The two rules are two files, one for each event. Together they leave the species hurt or fainted.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule keep_hurt on heal.hp
    when event.source == 2 && species[event.mon] == 25
    do refuse
recipes.rule2:
language 1
rule keep_fainted on mon.revive
    when event.source >= 3 && species[event.mon] == 25
    do refuse
notes: The first block is the rule for `heal.hp`; the second is the rule for `mon.revive`. Revive sources 3, 4 and 5 are the party heals: a Centre, the HP-restore power and any other script.

recipes.title: No experience from battles
recipes.goal: Nobody gains experience from a battle.
steps: `battle.exp` fires once when the battle hands out experience. Refused, nobody gains and `mon.exp` does not fire.
Add a guard such as `event.wild == 1` to limit it to wild battles.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_battle_exp on battle.exp
    do refuse

recipes.title: One Pokemon gains no experience
recipes.goal: Pokemon of species 25 gain nothing from battles; the rest gain as usual.
steps: `mon.exp` fires once for each member that gains. Setting `event.amount` to 0 gives that member none.
`battle.exp` is the whole hand-out; use it to stop everyone, and `mon.exp` to pick members.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_exp_pikachu on mon.exp
    when species[event.mon] == 25 && event.source == 0
    do set event.amount 0

recipes.title: Nothing comes back from fainting
recipes.goal: A fainted Pokemon stays fainted: no revive item, move, Centre or script heal brings it back.
steps: `mon.revive` fires for every way a fainted Pokemon comes back, and it can be refused. A rule with no guard refuses them all.
At a party heal the event fires once for each fainted member, and a refusal leaves only that member fainted. The others are healed.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_revives on mon.revive
    do refuse
notes: The Pokemon Centre's nurse runs the same script command as other script heals, so the port reports both as source 5 and a rule cannot tell them apart.

recipes.title: Check types in the party
recipes.goal: Refuse a ball on a species without a type, and refuse wild encounters while the party has no Pokemon of that type.
steps: Type ids are the game's own: Water is 10.
`species_type1[s]` and `species_type2[s]` read a species' types. The first rule refuses the ball when neither is Water.
`party_has_type[t]` is 1 when a party Pokemon that is not an egg has type `t`. The second rule refuses the encounter when it is 0.
A rule file holds one rule, so these are two files.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule water_only on catch.attempt
    when species_type1[event.species] != 10 && species_type2[event.species] != 10
    do refuse
    do message "Only Water types."
recipes.rule2:
language 1
rule need_water on encounter.wild
    when party_has_type[10] == 0
    do refuse
notes: The first block is the rule for `catch.attempt`; the second is the rule for `encounter.wild`.

recipes.title: Use the play time
recipes.goal: Wild encounters start only after the save has an hour of play time.
steps: `play_seconds` is the play time of the save in seconds.
`encounter.wild` can be refused. The player keeps walking.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule slow_start on encounter.wild
    when play_seconds < 3600
    do refuse

recipes.title: Stronger second Pokemon in dark grass
recipes.goal: In a double battle from dark grass, the second wild Pokemon is two levels higher.
steps: `event.method` is 1 for dark grass and `event.double` is 1 for a double battle.
`event.level2` and `event.species2` are the second Pokemon of the double. Both are writable. `level2` is 0 when there is no second Pokemon.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule dark_grass_pair on encounter.wild
    when event.method == 1 && event.double == 1
    do add event.level2 2

recipes.title: Change a trainer's party
recipes.goal: Every Pokemon of every trainer is a number of levels higher, and the player picks the number.
steps: `battle.trainer_mon` fires once for each opposing Pokemon, in party order, after the game builds the party.
A new level works out the stats again. Writing 0 to `level`, `species` or `ability` keeps the game's value.
The option is a whole number. `setting.boost` reads it. It is declared in the options file with a lowest value, a highest value and a default.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule stronger_trainers on battle.trainer_mon
    do add event.level setting.boost

recipes.title: Change experience by source
recipes.goal: Wild battles give no experience.
steps: `event.source` is 0 for a battle and 1 for the day care.
`event.wild` is 1 when the battle is a wild one.
The event fires once for each member that gains experience, and an amount of 0 gives that member none.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule no_grinding on mon.exp
    when event.source == 0 && event.wild == 1
    do set event.amount 0

recipes.title: Move a Pokemon to a box
recipes.goal: A Pokemon of the player that faints is moved to box 23.
steps: `box <mon> <n>` moves a party Pokemon to box `n`, counted from 0. It is applied at the next field step, so the battle is not disturbed.
It fails when the box is full, and it never leaves the party without a Pokemon that is not an egg.
recipes.rule:
language 1
rule graveyard on battle.faint
    when event.side == 0
    do box event.mon 23

recipes.title: Count faints of all players
recipes.goal: Show the faints of every player together in the status panel.
steps: The manifest needs a `multiplayer = 1` line so the mod takes part in multiplayer.
The handler also runs for other players' events. `event_player` is 0 for this game's own, so each faint is added once, by the game it happens in.
The total is a number in the shared table. `shared_add` adds 1 on the host, in the order the faints arrive, so every faint counts.
`shared_get` returns 0 when the key is set. It reads the total the host has sent.

recipes.title: Log another player's catch
recipes.goal: Show a line when another player catches a Pokemon.
steps: The manifest needs a `multiplayer = 1` line so the mod takes part in multiplayer.
`event_player` is 0 for this game's own catches, else the player's number.
`event.caught` is 1 when the catch succeeded.
